lessons.principle: A visual beat is clearest when a stable state changes through a visible action into a new stable state.
lessons.application: Represent technique shots as state_from, action, and state_to with a readable contact phase.
constraints: Every action phase changes silhouette, contact, center of mass, camera, or overlay.
Hold the resulting state long enough to inspect it.

lessons.principle: Persistent subject colors, screen direction, and support points make intertwined motion legible.
lessons.application: Keep practitioner ownership and the mat frame stable through close-ups and transitions.
constraints: A close-up retains at least one ownership cue.
A spatial reset is explicit rather than accidental.

lessons.principle: Each framing answers one visual question before the next framing changes the question.
lessons.application: Use a stable set of shot functions: setup, contact, transition, comparison, diagram, and result.
constraints: Do not repeat one framing for more than two consecutive shots.
Use a wide view before detail views when ownership is ambiguous.

lessons.principle: A useful diagram reveals hidden structure on top of the action and then returns control to the action.
lessons.application: Attach force arrows, fulcrums, and load markers to reviewed body contacts.
constraints: An overlay has an anchored origin and direction.
The diagram cannot introduce an unsupported body position.

lessons.principle: The decisive grip, frame, or support contact receives the strongest local contrast.
lessons.application: Isolate one contact target while preserving the larger cast silhouette.
constraints: Contact accents are bounded to the reviewed target.
An accent never changes practitioner identity.

lessons.principle: A transition feels continuous when a shape, path, or anchor persists into the next shot.
lessons.application: Carry a body arc, mat line, grip marker, or force arrow across a cut or diagram reveal.
constraints: The inherited anchor is named in the treatment.
A hard reset is reserved for a documented chapter change.

lessons.principle: Visual density increases only when the lesson adds a causal relationship.
lessons.application: Keep the field quiet for setup and add labels or overlays at the moment they explain change.
constraints: No decorative overlay competes with an instructional contact.
Labels recede after the causal moment.

lessons.principle: Different force paths read better when their curves and accents are distinguishable.
lessons.application: Use distinct motion tokens for linear drive, pivot, compression, and release.
constraints: A force token is selected by the reviewed action.
Motion accents remain subordinate to anatomy and contact.

observations.signal: Short physical exchanges remain readable when each cut carries a causal state change.
observations.design_rule: Shorten shots around contact and consequence while preserving a result hold.

observations.signal: A sparse visual field can hold attention when its geometry changes continuously.
observations.design_rule: Reveal diagram primitives only when they explain a force, support, or trajectory.

observations.signal: Repeated layouts teach the viewer where to look for labels, actors, and outcomes.
observations.design_rule: Reuse composition roles while varying state, action, and focal target.
